freeAlt.title: Free alternatives to paid tools
freeAlt.intro: Some tools mentioned on this page are paid, rate-limited or restricted in Uzbekistan. All assignments can be completed in full with the following free tools:
freeAlt.alt1: — instead use: Microsoft Designer (Bing Image Creator), image generation in the free tiers of Gemini or ChatGPT, Stable Diffusion; for precise scientific drawings — Inkscape, diagrams.net, GeoGebra.
freeAlt.alt2: — instead use: screen-record your own Canvas simulation with OBS Studio, animate in Manim (Python) or Blender, edit in Shotcut/Kdenlive.
freeAlt.alt3: — instead use: Manim, Blender, or record the simulation with OBS Studio — this yields a physically accurate video.
freeAlt.alt4: — instead use: Manim, Blender, OBS Studio.
freeAlt.alt5: — instead use: the browser Web Speech API, the Uzbek voices of Microsoft Edge “Read aloud”, or record your own voice with Audacity.
freeAlt.alt6: — instead use: Web Speech API, Microsoft Edge Uzbek voices; Whisper for transcription.
freeAlt.alt7: — instead use: Web Speech API (no account or payment card required).
freeAlt.alt8: — instead use: Whisper — open source, supports Uzbek, runs free of charge in Google Colab.

textbook.lead: The textbook comprises 15 lectures, 15 laboratory works, 3 supplementary astronomy topics and appendices.

plan.lead: Unite theory, imagery, animation and coding in a single project workflow.

card2.title: Lesson script

lectures.title: 15 lectures
lectures.lead: Every lecture includes theory, worked examples and AI integration.

card1.title: The paradigm of creating physics simulation animations with AI
card1.text: An approach to working with artificial intelligence in the digital era.

card2.title: Methodology of modelling a physical process
card2.text: Stages of modelling and the foundations of scientific methodology.

card3.title: The ecosystem of modern artificial intelligence tools
card3.text: The role and potential of AI tools in the learning process.

card4.title: Requirements for a computer model and computational accuracy
card4.text: Numerical methods and criteria for assessing model accuracy.

card5.title: Modelling physical processes as a method of cognition
card5.text: Types of models and their place in the theory of knowledge.

card6.title: Building physical models with digital technologies
card6.text: Free-body diagrams, force vectors and algorithmic flowcharts.

card7.text: The frame loop, delta-time integration and Retina high-DPI scaling.

card8.title: Programming physics with AI: vectors, forces, collisions
card8.text: Vector arithmetic, Newton’s laws and the impulse of 2D elastic collisions.

card9.title: Code generation with artificial intelligence and prompt engineering
card9.text: Zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought strategies and professional prompt architecture.

card10.title: Visualising physical and astronomical data
card10.text: Keplerian orbital mechanics, coordinate transformations and audio-visual synchronisation.

card11.title: Designing a physics course on distance-learning platforms
card11.text: LMS architecture, Otter.ai transcription, adaptive pathways in MagicSchool AI and portfolio audit in Google Antigravity.

card12.title: Modelling and animating the laws of mechanics
card12.text: Newtonian dynamics, the impulse of 2D elastic collisions and the PhET→Claude→Antigravity→Runway AI pipeline.

card13.title: Modelling and animating the laws of thermodynamics
card13.text: The Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution, Carnot/Stirling cycles and P–V/T–S phase diagrams.

card14.title: Modelling and simulating the laws of electrodynamics
card14.text: Coulomb fields, Faraday induction, RLC circuits and audio-narration synthesis with Muxlisa AI/ElevenLabs.

card15.title: Laws of nuclear physics and the methodology of the independent capstone project
card15.text: Radioactive decay, the U-235 fission chain reaction, D–T fusion and a capstone project built on a 7-stage AI pipeline.

independent.title: 15 independent-study assignments — 60 hours
independent.lead: Cards in the same format as lectures and labs: open any topic to see model guidelines, a worked example and study materials. Official submission and grading take place in HEMIS.

card1.title: AI and the paradigm of physics education
card1.text: Write a scientific-analytical article on the impact of generative AI tools on physics education and the changes ahead.

card2.text: Develop a step-by-step methodology and flowchart for modelling a chosen complex physical process with an LLM.

card3.title: Comparative analysis of the AI ecosystem
card3.text: A comparative analysis of three AI tools’ ability to write code and build physics simulations.

card4.title: Numerical integration and computational errors
card4.text: Study the errors of numerical integration methods such as Euler and Runge–Kutta in physics simulations and prepare a presentation on computational stability.

card5.title: A portfolio of deterministic and stochastic models
card5.text: Find real-life examples of deterministic and stochastic models and write a report on the algorithms that represent them on a computer.

card6.title: Digitising a free-body diagram
card6.text: Construct the force-vector system of a complex mechanical system and render it schematically with AI image generators.

card7.title: Free-fall animation with HTML5 Canvas
card7.text: Analyse the code of a free-fall animation in JavaScript and HTML5 Canvas and explain the frame-update logic.

card8.title: A computational module for elastic collisions
card8.text: Create, with AI assistance, a small Python or JavaScript module that computes elastic collisions, and write out the physical equations.

card9.title: A prompt-engineering guide for physics
card9.text: Compile a library of purpose-built prompts that let physics teachers obtain code and lesson scripts from AI.

card10.title: Visualisation of astronomical data
card10.text: Build an interactive chart from an open astronomical database and draw conclusions.

card11.title: A four-week distance physics course
card11.text: Design the structure, materials and assessment criteria of a four-week online physics module for Google Classroom or Moodle LMS.

card12.title: A set of tasks based on a mechanics simulation
card12.text: Analyse ready-made simulation code that demonstrates the laws of kinematics or dynamics and create a set of practical tasks for school pupils.

card13.title: A methodological guide to thermodynamic modelling
card13.text: Prepare a fragment of a teaching guide on algorithms for the numerical modelling of Brownian motion or the ideal-gas state.

card14.title: A lesson plan in electrodynamics
card14.text: Prepare a comprehensive lesson plan explaining Faraday’s law or magnetic field lines using the PhET or Vascak visual laboratories.

card15.title: Concept of a nuclear physics model
card15.text: Develop and defend, as a script or business plan, a computer-model project for teaching a nuclear phenomenon such as radioactive decay interactively.

labs.title: 15 laboratory works
labs.lead: Every laboratory work includes theory, worked examples and AI integration.

card1.title: Creating an initial visual design of physics simulation animations with artificial intelligence tools
card1.text: A 6-stage MagicSchool → Gemini/ChatGPT → Midjourney → Runway/Sora → Claude AI pipeline and a capstone rubric.

card2.title: Building the mathematical model, formulas and algorithm of a chosen physical process in logical order with an LLM
card2.text: Reverse engineering of PhET/Vascak.cz → formula checking in Claude → an IMRaD report in Gemini/ChatGPT, an Euler–Cromer test bench and a 100-point rubric.

card3.title: Registering in the modern AI ecosystem and setting up an integrated virtual workspace for a physics lesson
card3.text: Practical mini-tasks on 7 AI tools, a Canva AI / Midjourney pipeline infographic, a live ecosystem tracker and a 100-point rubric.

card4.title: Testing the computational accuracy of computer models in WolframAlpha and AI (Code Interpreter) and plotting error graphs
card4.text: Euler, Euler–Cromer and RK4 methods on a pendulum, the integration step and error convergence, a live test bench and a 100-point rubric.

card5.title: Comparing and visually analysing deterministic and stochastic models through computer simulations
card5.text: PhET “Gravity and Orbits” and “Gas Properties”, an 8-criterion comparison table, a parallel orbit/gas bench and a 100-point rubric.

card6.title: Constructing a free-body diagram (a system of force vectors) and drawing it with AI image generators (Midjourney/DALL-E)
card6.text: An inclined-plane FBD, Coulomb–Amontons friction, Claude Vision analysis, Euler–Cromer pseudocode, an interactive FBD bench and a 100-point rubric.

card7.title: Coding an animation of simple physical oscillations with HTML5 Canvas and JavaScript, accounting for frame rate (delta-time)
card7.text: requestAnimationFrame, the Fiedler accumulator, an Euler–Cromer oscillator, Google Antigravity monitoring, an FPS/delta-time bench and a 100-point rubric.

card8.title: Writing a small physics engine based on elastic collisions and vector arithmetic through pair programming with AI
card8.text: Vector2D, the impulse scalar J and overlap resolution, Driver/Navigator debugging with Claude, a Monte Carlo check in Code Interpreter, a collision arena and a 100-point rubric.

card9.title: Writing targeted prompts for code generation, comparing them and building a personal prompt library for physics
card9.text: Zero-shot → constrained → Role + CoT → XML master prompt, a 4-level pendulum sandbox, a phase portrait, a personal prompt library and a 100-point rubric.

card10.title: Visualising interactive plots of body trajectories from physical and astronomical databases
card10.text: NASA JPL orbital elements, Kepler’s laws and equation, TTS (Muxlisa, ElevenLabs, Google Cloud) and SSML, an audio–animation synchronisation bench and a rubric.

card11.title: Creating an AI-assisted digital physics course and publishing its content on LMS platforms (Google Classroom, Moodle)
card11.text: Otter.ai transcription and WER, adaptive assessment (the Rasch model), MagicSchool AI, an LMS integration simulator and a 100-point rubric.

card12.title: Modelling mechanical dynamics (Newton’s laws) in Algodoo or with AI-written code and rendering kinematic videos
card12.text: Newton’s laws and momentum conservation, Vascak.cz/PhET analysis, a physics engine built with Claude and Antigravity, a 3D elastic-collision bench and a presentation rubric.

card13.title: Writing a simulation of thermodynamic processes (P–V and T–S diagrams, ideal-gas state) and analysing the visual change of state
card13.text: The ideal-gas equation of state, P–V and T–S diagrams, a particle-based stochastic gas simulation, a live P–V bench and a rubric.

card14.title: Creating interactive code that models electromagnetic fields and electric circuits and narrating the process with AI
card14.text: Electromagnetic induction and electric circuits, an interactive model that responds to magnet motion, AI narration (TTS) and a rubric.

card15.title: Building a complete simulator of nuclear phenomena (radioactive decay) and the final defence of integrating all AI tools
card15.text: The law of radioactive decay, half-life, a stochastic nuclei simulator and the decay curve, and the final defence of integrating all AI tools.

card2.title: Spectral analysis
card2.text: Planck’s, Wien’s and the Stefan–Boltzmann laws, the Balmer series, the Doppler shift and Hubble’s law; a CD spectroscope and SDSS spectra.

card3.title: Telescope observation data
card3.text: Photometry, light curves, period finding, Cepheid distances and transits; open Kepler and TESS data.

This site creates no accounts and awards no grades.

sims.stableEnd: Stable nucleus — the series is complete.
sims.fusionNote: * The stage-1 energy includes the annihilation of the positron with an electron; part of it (≈ 0.26 MeV on average) is carried away by the neutrino. In the real Sun, stage 1 is extremely slow because it proceeds via the weak interaction (billions of years per proton on average); for clarity this model speeds up all reaction rates while preserving their relative order (stage 1 is the slowest) and their strong temperature dependence.
sims.seriesNote: α decay: A → A−4, Z → Z−2 (down-left on the chart). β⁻ decay: A is unchanged, Z → Z+1, N → N−1 (up-left, not right). Half-lives: NUBASE2020 data (rounded). Minor branchings of the series are not shown; for the thorium series the main (64%) β⁻ branch of Bi-212 is given.
sims.lorentzTheory: F = q(E + v × B). With B alone, the force is perpendicular to the velocity: it does no work, the speed stays constant and the particle moves in a circle. Adding E makes the circle drift along E × B with velocity v<sub>d</sub> = E/B.
sims.lorentzNote: The computation uses the Boris method, which conserves the speed exactly in a pure magnetic field. A positive charge circulates clockwise, a negative one counter-clockwise. A plain Euler method would turn the circle into a growing spiral.
